title: Joining Duke for one night: Worcester broadcast, Providence, then the Paramount
summary: Duke called him to replace Otto Hardwick for a Worcester broadcast and a dance; he was gradually persuaded to stay, was hired after about ten days and asked about pay.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, you know the old story about joining Duke for one night and staying 28 years. Well, that's a fact, because
he called me to play this important Saturday afternoon broadcast in Worcester, Massachusetts. So I went there. I went up to Massachusetts that afternoon and played the broadcast with him, and --

And I played the broadcast, and he said, 'Well, since you're here we're playing a dance tonight in Providence, Rhode Island. Why don't you come and play with us?' So I said, 'Okay, since I'm up here in New England.' You know. I mean I wasn't too anxious to join Duke, you know, as such, you know.

Right then. Right then at that moment, because it meant leaving home again, which I had just got out of the Army and I'd been away from home a little bit. But incidentally, the longest I was away from home when I was in the Army was eight months. That's the longest period I was away from home.

So when I joined Duke, you know, it was sort of I had to make a decision. I wanted to, you know, get back on my feet, you know, and have some money in my pocket and whatnot. So I decided, well, I said to my -- if he offered me the -- he hadn't offered me the job. I was just filling in for

someone else, Otto Hardwick. So one word led to another and so he was playing New England and he was coming back to New York. So we talked from day to day. So I decided that, well, I'd just finish this little trip, then I'd be back home, you know. Then I discovered he was going to play the Paramount (Laughs) Theater for six weeks. / So one day we were up in Hartford. There was a theater all the bands used to play on Sunday. I think it was the Star Theater, the Star Theater. All the bands, you know, they'd have a big show on Sunday, just one day. They'd have singers, you know, acts. So he called me. Then he really talked to me then. He said, 'I'll tell you what. I don't know whether this guy, Hardwick, I don't know where he is, and --,' I think he called him a nut or something else. He said, 'I don't know what this nut's going to do.' So he said, 'Why don't you stay? Why don't you stay with us.' You know, 'I think you'd like it.' 'Yeah, well, how much would you want?' You know, that sort of thing. And I told him. And he agreed, okay, you know. So I was hired. And this was after I'd been in the band about 10 days. So I remember after about five days or so, I said, you know, by that time I was talking. I had got the lay of the land, and I was sitting about the fourth seat back, Duke sat up in the front seat, and I said, 'Hey, Duke.' And he said, 'Huh?' And I said, 'Who's supposed to pay me?'
